scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a claim response that concedes why heroism seems impossible today, then refutes it; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: We live surrounded by news that quickly turns admired figures into targets of criticism.
Some people claim that it is no longer possible for a society to regard any living man or woman as a hero.
I disagree with this claim, because genuine heroes still exist, even though admiration is harder to keep today.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why the claim seems convincing

sentences.text: First, it is worth admitting why this claim seems convincing to many people.
Modern media expose the private faults of famous people more completely than ever before.
For example, once-admired stars and leaders are often disgraced when their hidden failings appear in the news.
This shows that public admiration can collapse the moment a serious flaw is revealed.
Constant criticism online can also tear down almost any reputation in a matter of days.
In such a climate, lasting heroes can seem harder to find than they once were.
To this extent, the claim points to a real change in how we view famous people.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why the claim goes too far

sentences.text: Second, however, the claim that no living hero is possible simply goes too far.
A hero is admired not for being flawless but for real courage, kindness, or self-sacrifice.
Consider the rescue workers and volunteers who risk their lives in disasters and are deeply admired by all.
Such acts earn lasting respect that no amount of media attention can erase.
Many living people, from doctors to activists, are still widely seen as heroes today.
Knowing that heroes are human and imperfect can make their courage even more inspiring.
Genuine heroism, then, remains entirely possible in our own time.
In conclusion, intense media coverage does make admiration harder to sustain.
But it has not made heroes impossible, since true courage and goodness still earn deep respect.
We can still recognise living heroes, as long as we honour real virtue rather than expect perfection.
